title: The Fake Average
covers: choosing between mean and median based on outliers and data shape (symmetric vs. skewed)
cert: choosing the best measure of center (mean or median) when outliers or skew are present

intro.caption: Lesson 2-10 — choose appropriate measures. Max Maxwell is bragging to sponsors about his '200K average views'! Clip Squad goes on a fact-checking quest to judge his claim.

balloons.t: Max told the sponsors his clips average 200K views! Chat is losing its mind!
I pulled his last five clips: 12K, 15K, 14K, 19K, and 940K. Look at that last one!
Add 'em up: 1,000K divided by 5 is 200K! Totally typical!
Four clips are under 20K! That ONE 940K viral clip is an OUTLIER dragging the mean up!

pages.caption: An outlier is a value far away from the rest of the data. It pulls the mean toward itself, even when most values are nowhere near it.

balloons.t: Check Max's numbers yourself. One extreme spike changes the whole mean.
Sort the five clips first! The MEDIAN ignores how giant that 940K spike is.
12, 14, 15, 19, 940 — the middle one is way closer to a normal clip!
When data is symmetric with NO outliers, the mean is great!
When data is SKEWED or has an outlier, pick the median!
Fine, try my sponsor earnings: $10, $15, $12, $13, $950! Still a $200 average!
Sponsors want the truth, Max. Judge the claim with the right measure!
Fake average exposed! Sponsors signed with Clip Squad instead — no outlier tricks needed!

win.caption: Use the mean for symmetric data with no outliers; use the median when an outlier or skewed shape pulls the mean away from typical.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Spot the Outlier
gates.prompt: Inspect Max's five clip view counts (in thousands): 12, 15, 14, 19, 940.
hints: Conceptual: an outlier sits far apart from the main cluster of data.
Procedural: compare all 5 numbers to spot the extreme one, then add all 5 and divide by 5 to see what it does to the mean.

steps: Four values sit between 8 and 11; 62 is far away — so 62 is the outlier.
worked.q: Which number is the outlier in 4, 6, 5, 7, 78?

items.label: In 12, 15, 14, 19, 940 (thousands), which value is the outlier?

fb.msg: 12 sits right next to 14, 15, and 19. Look for the value far away from the cluster.
200 is the mean, not one of the five clip values.
15 is right in the middle of the cluster, not an outlier.

items.fbDefault: Pick the single value in 12, 15, 14, 19, 940 that is far from all the others.

items.label: What mean (in thousands) does Max get for 12, 15, 14, 19, 940?

fb.msg: 1000 is the total views. Divide by 5 clips to get the mean!
15 is the median, not the mean.

gates.pass: 940K is the outlier, and it drags the mean up to 200K — higher than 4 out of 5 clips!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Pick the Measure
gates.prompt: Find the median of Max's clips and decide which measure of center is fairer.
hints: Conceptual: the median depends on order, not size — one giant spike cannot drag it upward.
Procedural: sort the numbers from least to greatest first, then pick the middle number.

steps: Sort: 45, 48, 50, 52, 55, 260. Middle pair is 50 and 52 → median = $51.
$260 is an outlier pulling the mean to $85, so the median ($51) is fairer.

items.label: Median of 12, 15, 14, 19, 940 (sort least to greatest first!):

fb.msg: 14 is in the middle BEFORE sorting! Sort least to greatest: 12, 14, 15, 19, 940.
200 is the mean, not the median.
940 is the maximum, not the middle value.

items.fbDefault: Sort 12, 14, 15, 19, 940 and pick the middle value.

items.q: Which measure best describes Max's typical clip (12K, 15K, 14K, 19K, 940K)?

options.t: Mean (200K), because it uses every number in the list
options.fb: Using every number lets the 940K outlier pull the mean to 200K — higher than 4 of the 5 clips!

options.t: Median (15K), because the 940K outlier pulls the mean way above normal clips
Mean (200K), because bigger averages sound better
options.fb: A fair measure describes what is typical, not what sounds flashiest.

options.t: Median (14K), because 14 is in the middle before sorting
options.fb: Always sort first! Sorted 12, 14, 15, 19, 940 has median 15K.

gates.pass: 15K! That's the real story of Max's channel.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Shape Decides
gates.prompt: Match the best measure of center to each data set's shape.
hints: Conceptual: symmetric data with no outliers balances nicely around the mean; skewed data or outliers pull the mean toward the tail.
Procedural: check for any extreme value or long tail. Outlier or skew → median. Symmetric, no outlier → mean.

steps: Set A: 20, 22, 21, 19, 23 → clustered evenly, no outliers → mean (21) works great.
Set B: 20, 22, 21, 19, 98 → 98 skews the data high → median (21) is better.
worked.q: Which measure is better for skewed data with an extreme high value: mean or median?

items.q: Clip Squad's last 5 videos got 28K, 30K, 29K, 31K, 32K views (symmetric, no outliers). Which measure fits best?

options.t: Only 32K, because it is the highest
options.fb: 32K is the maximum, not a measure of center.

options.t: Mean (30K), because the data is symmetric with no outliers
Neither, because the numbers are too close together
options.fb: Closely clustered symmetric data is ideal for the mean!

items.q: Six sponsor offers are $15, $18, $16, $17, $15, $72. Which measure best represents a typical offer?

options.t: Mean, because $72 is part of the data
options.fb: $72 is a huge outlier that pulls the mean to $25.50 — higher than 5 of the 6 offers!

options.t: Mean, because there are an even number of offers
options.fb: Even vs. odd count does not decide mean vs. median — outliers and skew do!

options.t: Median, because $72 is an outlier that skews the data

gates.pass: Symmetric → mean; skewed or outlier → median! Clip Squad takes the evidence board to the sponsor booth.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Expose the Claim
gates.prompt: Judge Max's final sponsor claim and lock in the rule for choosing mean vs. median.
hints: Conceptual: a fair measure of center sits near the bulk of the data, not out in a tail.
Procedural: sort the data to find the median, check if an outlier is distorting the mean, and justify your choice.

steps: The outlier 74 pulls the mean to 20, so median (7) is the fairer measure.

items.q: Lock 1 · Max's 5 streams earned $10, $15, $12, $13, $950. He claims a typical stream earns $200. Does his claim hold?

options.t: Yes — $200 is the exact mean, so it is typical
options.fb: The mean is $200, but 4 out of 5 streams earned $15 or less! That is not typical.

options.t: No — $950 is an outlier pulling the mean to $200, while typical is near the median ($13)
No — the median is $12, the middle of the unsorted list
options.fb: Sort first: $10, $12, $13, $15, $950 has a median of $13, not $12.

items.label: Lock 2 · Median of $10, $15, $12, $13, $950:

fb.msg: 200 is the mean, pulled up by $950.
950 is the outlier, not the median.

items.fbDefault: Sort 10, 12, 13, 15, 950 and pick the middle value.

items.q: Lock 3 · When is the mean better than the median?

options.t: When one huge outlier pulls the average up
options.fb: That is when you should use the MEDIAN.

options.t: When the data is heavily skewed to one side
options.fb: Skewed data pulls the mean toward the tail — use the median!

options.t: When the data is roughly symmetric with no outliers
Whenever you want the biggest possible number
options.fb: Pick the measure that fairly describes the data, not the biggest number.

gates.pass: CLAIM BUSTED! $13 median vs. $200 fake average — the sponsors walk away from Max's booth!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-10 — what the fake average taught us
rows: An outlier sits far from the rest of the data and pulls the mean toward itself.
When data has an outlier or is skewed, the median resists the pull and shows what is typical.
When data is roughly symmetric with no outliers, the mean is a great summary.
Always order the values from least to greatest before finding the median.
journal.quote: "One viral spike does not make every Tuesday a hit." — Nova

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-10 (Choose Appropriate Measures) as one focused read. Covers spotting outliers, seeing how outliers pull the mean, and choosing between mean and median based on symmetry vs. skew.
standards: Relate the choice of measures of center and variability to the shape of the data distribution
